description: Validator unit test: sk_live_, sk_test_, rk_live_, rk_test_ accepted; pk_, empty, whitespace-only, random text rejected
connectStripeAction rejects a bad secret-key format server-side before calling Stripe, even when the form check is bypassed
connectStripeAction with a fake client where every permission is granted: connects, stores key, creates webhook, sk_ and rk_ behave identically
connectStripeAction with webhook_write denied: fails, stores nothing (no secret, no config row change), error names webhook_write and the webhooks capability
connectStripeAction with only saved-card/import permissions denied: connects, returns those capabilities unavailable with permission names
Permission-error translation unit test using the real SDK error shape recorded by the spike (type, code, message) and a StripeAuthenticationError for an invalid key
Reconnect regression: Update API keys on a connected tenant keeps webhook endpoint id, signing secret and every saved payment setting (extend connectStripeAction.reconnect.test.ts)
Connection settings render test: connected state shows Update API keys; key help lists manifest permissions
Drift test: every Stripe SDK call in the three files is covered by the manifest; adding an uncovered call makes it fail
Docs table and manifest agree (test compares the permission ids in the docs file with the manifest)
Locale test: every locale file has the new strings and none still says the key must start with sk_

Manual end-to-end against Stripe test mode with an rk_test_ key holding exactly the manifest permissions: connect, pay a Checkout link and see the invoice paid via webhook, save a card, auto-pay charge, import customers; then remove each of webhook_write, checkout_session_write, payment_intent_write, customer_read in turn and see the named error. Results recorded in SCRATCHPAD.md
